sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: Chapter 13, Section 13.2, printed pp. 109–111 (PDF pp. 122–124); Appendix B.2, finite repetition/error reduction. The separate sequential full-document reading receipt is qc_r3.

contents.name: Circuit families and uniformity
contents.support: Supports polynomially describable circuit families and the indexed-gate query convention. QC14 explicitly adopts full-list generation and makes no indexed-to-list equivalence claim.

contents.name: BQP and bounded error
contents.support: Supports the standard bounded-error circuit-class interface and ordinary repetition intuition; the promise and full-list details are fixed locally.

contents.name: Acceptance model
contents.support: Supports finite circuit computation and measured acceptance at a broad level; no partial-output or POVM proof is imported.

contents.name: Complexity-class error reduction
contents.support: States repetition and majority as an error-reduction route. The local proof supplies the independent-run tail bound, full-list construction, and charged resource counts.

contents.name: Error-robustness context
contents.support: Supports standard BQP thresholds and constant-error reduction. Its discussion of indexed uniformity and classical-separation beliefs is not adopted as a theorem.

contents.name: Circuit-family and computation cost vector
contents.support: Supports polynomial-time circuit-family context and ordinary gate-size discussion. The description, query, classical-bit, precision, and ancilla vector is a local refinement, not a source theorem.

contents.name: Uniform family-size context
contents.support: The source footnote uses indexed-gate access. QC14 proves only the full-list output bound and makes no indexed-to-list conversion claim.

contents.name: Partial-output normalization and POVM identification
contents.support: The source uses a measured output bit. It does not prove the local arbitrary-output-register marginal law; the assigned theorem supplies the finite Parseval and trace argument.

contents.name: Off-promise finite BQP example
contents.support: The chapter treats language inputs rather than the exact promise convention. The example uses the root promise-problem definition and local acceptance calculation; this source is context only.

reading_record.beta_inspection: Inspected the local full-text extraction for PDF pp. 122–124 and Appendix B.2 on 2026-10-16; Chapter 13 gives an indexed-gate footnote and only a repetition proof sketch, so the full-list bound and Chernoff proof are local.

sources.title: John Watrous, Quantum Computational Complexity, arXiv:0804.3401v1
sources.locator: Section IV.1, PDF pp. 12–13 (promise pair, generated circuits and BQP acceptance); Section IV.2, PDF p. 13 (Proposition 3 error reduction). The separate sequential full-document reading receipt is qc_r3.

contents.name: Promise problems and BQP thresholds
contents.support: Defines quantum acceptance on a disjoint YES/NO promise pair with no off-promise condition; QC14 adapts the acceptance semantics locally.

contents.name: Generated circuit families and BQP
contents.support: Supports polynomial-time-generated circuit families and the conventional BQP definition; the exact full-list code and gate alphabet are fixed locally.

contents.name: Acceptance and bounded-error class
contents.support: Supports acceptance thresholds 2/3 and 1/3 and the promise-problem formulation.

contents.name: Repetition error-reduction route
contents.support: Provides the repetition route. The procedure, rational threshold, computable repetition count, independent-run proof, and resource costs are supplied locally.

contents.name: Printed Proposition 3 equality
contents.support: The printed claim BQP(a,b)=BQP from inverse-polynomial gap alone is not used as proof: the endpoint case a=1,b=0 would assert exact bounded-error equivalence. QC14 proves the standard-threshold high-confidence equivalence locally and records this discrepancy for owner review.
contents.reason: The unrestricted gap-only equality printed in Proposition 3 is not adopted: endpoint thresholds (1,0) would assert an exact bounded-error equivalence. The approved QC14 robustness statement keeps its local standard-threshold/high-confidence proof and explicit generalized-threshold hypotheses.

contents.name: Circuit-family and computation cost vector
contents.locator: Sections III.2 and IV.1; current passage inspection included IV.1, PDF p.13
contents.support: Supports polynomially generated circuit families and ordinary complexity accounting. The complete description, separate query/classical-bit coordinates, precision encoding, and exact ancilla categories are fixed and justified locally; no larger QC14 cost vector is imported.

contents.name: Full-list output-length and width bound
contents.support: The local proof converts the fixed one-tape transition bound into a description-length, gate-count, and unary-wire-count bound; the source supplies the generated-family context, not the local encoding-count argument.

contents.name: Partial-output normalization and POVM identification
contents.locator: Sections III.2 and IV.1, including the one-output-qubit acceptance model
contents.support: Watrous gives the finite circuit acceptance model but not the local all-unmeasured-wires sum or POVM/partial-trace identification. These are proved directly from finite Parseval and the inspected partial-trace trace identity.

contents.name: Off-promise finite BQP example
contents.locator: Section I, PDF pp. 3–4, and Section IV.1, PDF p. 13
contents.support: Supports the disjoint promise-pair convention and standard BQP acceptance bounds. The identity-family witness and total predicate are verified locally.

reading_record.beta_inspection: Inspected the local full-text extraction for PDF pp. 12–14 and the promise-problem passage on pp. 3–4 on 2026-10-16; the IV.2 proposition and proof route were read in full. The page-specific full-document reread remains attributed to qc_r3.

canonical.name: Local unconditional phase invariance and controlled-phase witness
canonical.support: This canonical result is proved locally from squared amplitudes and explicit H/T matrices. Neither inspected complexity passage supplies this claim; the two former qualified source rows are recorded here once without attributing a phase theorem to either source.
